SAA-C03 validates the ability to design solutions on AWS based on the Well-Architected Framework. Scored content is weighted as follows:

  • Domain 1 — Design Secure Architectures: 30%
  • Domain 2 — Design Resilient Architectures: 26%
  • Domain 3 — Design High-Performing Architectures: 24%
  • Domain 4 — Design Cost-Optimized Architectures: 20%

Questions are scenario based: multiple choice and multiple response. Check the official exam guide for the current format and scoring.

lesson_title: AWS Solutions Architect Associate (SAA-C03) — full course (freeCodeCamp.org)

content:
• Use IAM roles (not access keys) for EC2, Lambda and cross-account access; apply least privilege
  • Use AWS Organizations with service control policies (SCPs) to set guardrails across accounts
  • Place databases and app servers in private subnets; use security groups (stateful, instance level) and network ACLs (stateless, subnet level)
  • Encrypt data at rest with AWS KMS and in transit with TLS (AWS Certificate Manager)
  • Protect web apps with AWS WAF and AWS Shield; store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager

• Spread instances across multiple Availability Zones behind an Elastic Load Balancer with an Auto Scaling group
  • Use Amazon RDS Multi-AZ for automatic database failover; read replicas scale reads
  • Decouple components with Amazon SQS (queues), Amazon SNS (pub/sub) and Amazon EventBridge (events)
  • Plan disaster recovery by RTO/RPO: backup & restore, pilot light, warm standby, multi-site active/active

• Storage: S3 for objects, EBS (gp3/io2) for block, EFS for shared Linux file systems, FSx for Windows/Lustre
  • Caching: Amazon ElastiCache for databases and sessions; CloudFront at the edge
  • Databases: Aurora for high-performance relational, DynamoDB (with DAX) for single-digit-millisecond NoSQL
  • Networking: Global Accelerator and CloudFront for global users; VPC endpoints for private access to AWS services

• Right-size instances and use Savings Plans/Reserved Instances for steady state, Spot for interruptible work
  • Use S3 lifecycle policies and S3 Intelligent-Tiering to move data to cheaper storage classes
  • Prefer serverless (Lambda, Fargate, DynamoDB on-demand) for spiky or low-volume workloads
  • Reduce data transfer costs with VPC gateway endpoints for S3/DynamoDB and CloudFront caching
